text:
Ah, the glorious dawn of adulthood, that magical era where the thrill of choosing between chicken and beef instant noodles rivals the excitement of a Nobel Prize ceremony. It is truly a time of profound spontaneity, where the most daring decision one makes is whether to binge-watch a show or simply stare at the ceiling while contemplating the structural integrity of one’s lower back.

In this brave new world of existential dread and mild indigestion, we find solace in the humble candle. Specifically, the primary material of a candle: wax. Yes, wax. The same substance that melts away under the slightest pressure, much like one’s resolve to exercise after a long day of paying bills. It is a fitting metaphor for our modern existence—solid on the surface, but destined to drip and pool into a messy, insignificant puddle if left unattended for too long. We light it not for warmth, but to pretend we have a cozy, curated aesthetic while we debate the merits of Netflix’s latest algorithmic suggestion. Truly, the pinnacle of human achievement.
